children: on Thursday said it is preparing to put its artificial-intelligence processors into orbit, taking an early step toward its long-term ambition of building computing infrastructure in space.

The company said that its Project Suncatcher research program will conduct its first in-orbit hardware test on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission, in collaboration with Planet. The prototype satellite will be used to assess how Google’s
Tensor Processing Units withstand launch stresses and the radiation and temperature conditions encountered in low Earth orbit.
said laboratory testing has shown its Trillium TPUs can tolerate radiation exposure above levels expected during a five-year mission. The hardware has also undergone simulated launch vibration tests.
Heat management is among the biggest obstacles to operating powerful processors in space. Because conventional air cooling is unavailable in a vacuum, Google
is evaluating heat pipes and radiators to move excess heat away from the chips.

The company envisions future satellites carrying multiple TPUs and communicating through laser-based links to form orbital computing clusters. A two-satellite test of the communications technology is planned for 2027.
said the initial mission is primarily intended to collect engineering data and identify problems that could shape later designs, rather than demonstrate a commercial system.

title: Google to test AI chips in space as Suncatcher project advances
